title: Retire what the reset orphaned
note: 67 guard scripts unreachable from run_guards.py, kept because 30+ live files still name their paths. Right call today, poor steady state. One bounded pass: delete with references, or record why it stays. NOT by bulk deletion -- the reference sweep IS the job. [!] SCOPE CORRECTED 2026-09-21: THE GUARD SCRIPTS WERE NOT THE ONLY ORPHAN, and the pattern is worth more than the list. The reset disarmed every workflow that WRITES to a retired register and swept none of the ones that READ one. A writer to a missing register fails loudly; a reader degrades to 'could not check' and keeps issuing advice about a file that is gone. Two were found the same day: (a) scope-overlap-audit.yml, which posted 'read the coordination board yourself' on the reset's own PR and is DISARMED in this pass; (b) scripts/ops/render_daily_brief.py + its test, five of whose six inputs were archived and whose guard (daily-brief-guard) was dropped in the same pass -- NOT deleted here, because A3 replaces it and removing a renderer before its replacement exists is how a capability goes missing quietly. [!] THE SWEEP THIS ROW OWES IS THEREFORE A READER SWEEP, not a deletion pass: for each path under docs/archive/2026-09-21-operating-reset/, find what still reads it. A grep for the archived FILENAMES across .github/ and scripts/ is the probe, and it needs a positive control -- the two above are it. [!] SCOPE WIDENED AGAIN 2026-09-21, and this one was found by the OPERATOR LOOKING AT THE PAGE rather than by my sweep -- which is the finding about the sweep. I scoped the reader hunt to .github/ and scripts/ and never looked at src/web/api/, so THE API THAT SERVES THE WORKFLOW PAGE still reads three archived registers and says so to the operator on every load: (a) a 'Live work sessions' panel reading docs/claude/work/SESSIONS.json, which degrades honestly to 'could not be read (absent)' but will never come back; (b) a WIP '0 / 8 in flight vs the declared ceiling' from the retired operating model; (c) THE WORK-STORE PANEL, which is the bad one -- src/web/api/routers/work.py:482-488 prints 'A bug to fix still goes to the review backlogs', instructing every reader to file into registers that are archived and unread. [!] THAT PANEL IS ACTIVE MISINFORMATION ON THE ONE PAGE BUILT TO PREVENT DROPPED WORK, so it outranks the rest of this row. It is a read path (Tier 1 per the tier table) but it is src/ and the route's tier must be checked against docs/api-tier-policy.md before editing. [!] THE LESSON FOR THE SWEEP ITSELF: 'grep the archived filenames' is the right probe but I ran it over the wrong POPULATION. The population is every consumer of an archived path ANYWHERE -- .github/, scripts/, src/, and the dashboard repo -- not the two directories I happened to be working in. [!] DISPATCHED 2026-09-21. MODEL UPGRADED haiku-4.5 -> sonnet-5, deliberately and against this row's own earlier value: this row's note records that the previous sweep ran over the WRONG POPULATION and that three of four orphan classes were found by something failing loudly or the operator looking at the page, not by the sweep. That is a judgement failure, not a throughput one, and haiku is the wrong instrument for it. The cheap-extraction half is instead being run SEPARATELY on the Fable pool as an independent cross-check (see E11) -- which gets the cheap model onto the cheap half without betting the sweep on it. [!] LANE TOLD the src/web/api/routers/work.py:482-488 panel OUTRANKS the 67 guard scripts, and that if budget runs short an honestly-bounded sweep REPORT beats a half-finished deletion pass. [!] THREE MORE INSTANCES FOUND ON 2026-09-21 WHILE THIS LANE WAS ALREADY RUNNING, all by running something rather than by a sweep, and they are FILED IN THE PIPELINE rather than added to this note so they cannot be lost if this lane lands without them: PI-20260921-0001 (trainer-VM serialization FIFO promised by two workflow comments, board archived -- routed to its own lane, session_01W7iGwkrozCQ8LYRSM8WgGE), PI-20260921-0002 (pr-landing-guard R13's first remedy message names the archived session-board.json, so every future Tier-1 self-landing PR is sent to a dead end before finding the working per-branch route), and PI-20260921-0003 (check_manager_scope.py derives WHO THE MANAGER IS from the archived MANAGER-LEASE.json, reports `no_manager_commits` on a branch with four manager commits, and EXITS 0 -- so the guard that enforces rule 1 of the manager contract fails OPEN while both CLAUDE.md and the manager SKILL still claim it is CI-enforced). [!] THE RUNNING TALLY IS NOW FIVE ORPHAN CLASSES AND FIVE FOUND THE HARD WAY. That is no longer an anecdote about one missed directory; it is evidence that a filename grep is the wrong PRIMARY probe. A guard or workflow that READS an archived register frequently does not name it in a greppable string at all -- it derives a path, or names it only in prose while the code reads a directory. The probe that actually caught 0002 and 0003 was RUNNING THE THING AND READING WHAT IT SAID. Consider adding that to this row's method: execute every guard in run_guards.py and every self-test, and treat `could not check`, `does not exist` and a green-on-nothing as findings. [!] CEILING BREACHED 2026-09-21: $22.73 against $20. Not killed -- the contract says read what the lane produced first, and the work is delivered in PR #12680. [!] BUT THE SWEEP IS INCOMPLETE and the Fable cross-check is how we know, which is exactly why E11 ran in parallel. E9 fixed the three Workflow-page panels (the operator-facing misinformation, which was the highest-value half and is done) and filed four pipeline rows, but did not reach the session-start hooks, CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL, the live-money runtime ping, or the five guards-reporting-clean-over-nothing. Those are filed rather than left in a PR body. NOT closed. [!] STATE CORRECTED AT CLOSE-OUT, 2026-09-21: this row was written `landed_unproven` while PR #12680 was still OPEN. That is simply wrong -- `landed_unproven` means MERGED with the effect not yet observed, and nothing here is merged. Set back to `in_flight`. Caught by close-out check 3, which is the check that exists for exactly this, and worth recording because the error runs in the DANGEROUS direction: a row reading `landed_unproven` tells the next session the code is on main and only the observation is outstanding, so it would not have looked for an unmerged PR. [!] STATE CORRECTED AT CLOSE-OUT: the row read `in_flight` against an archived lane. Its PR (#12680) is MERGED, but the row was always going to outlive it -- E11's independent Fable probe reached four live reader surfaces this sweep did not, and PI-20260921-0001's lane flagged ~20+ non-archived files still live-reading board-pointer.json / session-board.json. [!] SO IT IS `queued` WITH A SMALLER, SHARPER SCOPE than it started with, not `done`: the remaining population is the reader surfaces E9 missed, and the probe that found them was NOT a filename grep. Whoever takes it should start from docs/audits/archived-register-readers-fable-probe.md rather than re-running a sweep already shown to under-find.
